plan: Given my private value of $10, I should aim to bid below this to ensure a profit if I win. A bid of $5 maximizes the chance of winning while providing a profit margin, as other bidders might bid higher, given their own unknown values. With no prior history, this conservative approach balances winning chances and potential profit.

Given my value of $30, I want to maximize profit while ensuring a reasonable chance of winning. Bidding exactly $30 yields zero profit if I win. To balance winning and profit, I'll bid slightly lower, ensuring potential profit if I win, yet still competitive. A bid around $20 maximizes expected profit, as it leaves room for profit ($10) if I win, while being high enough to potentially outbid cautious bidders. This strategy considers that others might bid closer to their values but not exceed them significantly.

Given my private value of $25, I aim to maximize profit by winning with a bid lower than my value. A bid slightly above the midpoint (e.g., $12) balances winning chances and profit margin. With no prior rounds to consider, assume competitors bid randomly. A bid of $12 offers a good chance of winning while ensuring profit if successful.
